title: Private VPC load-balance orchestrator: AZ-aware conntrack + NLB->ALB target provisioning
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a Terraform module and rollout plan for Private (VPC) deployments that reliably provisions internal NLB/ALB ingress stacks with AZ-aware connection tracking (conntrack) tuning, robust health-check semantics, and a safe TLS termination/ACM rotation strategy. This ticket covers module design, Terraform lifecycle hooks for blue/green upgrades, testing harnesses, and runbook updates for on-prem and VPC-private installs.
description_long:
Background:
Customers running Redwood Private require an internal ingress that provides: (a) deterministic routing for model-serving endpoints, (b) TLS termination where mandated (but optionally re-encrypted to backends), and (c) predictable failover across AZs and capacity tiers. In prior rollouts we've observed cache invalidation and conntrack exhaustion during large canary/upgrade events which caused transient connection resets and 502s for stateful gRPC streams.

Scope (deliverables):
- Terraform module: sources/terraform/modules/private-lb with clear inputs for mode (ip | instance), scheme (internal), protocol chains (TLS passthrough | TLS terminate+reencrypt), and SNI/ALPN mappings.
- Conntrack orchestration helper: automated sysctl tuning recommendations (conntrack_max/timeouts) and optional bootstrap scripts (user-data) for customer AMIs or node pools.
- AZ-aware target registration: ensure target groups are created with cross-zone-aware weight distribution and attach targets in the same AZ as NLB targets to avoid cross-AZ SNAT/firewall asymmetry.
- Health check semantics: dual-probe approach (fast NLB tcp/ssl probe + ALB http(s) application probe) with retry/backoff policy to avoid flapping during rolling upgrades.
- Terraform upgrade strategy: lifecycle rules to create replacement target groups, staggered weight-shifting with automated guardrails, and plan-time checks for conntrack capacity.
- TLS/ACM lifecycle: support for ACM cert import/rotation for Private (bring-your-own cert) and automated validation hooks integrated with the console rollouts API.
- E2E tests: local integration in CI that simulates scale-up (1k concurrent connections) and rolling deploy scenarios; unit tests for the module inputs and plan validation.
- Runbook & docs: step-by-step upgrade runbook, failure modes, and mitigation steps (including forced rollback via route weights).

Out-of-scope: cross-account peering implementation and marketplace listings.

Implementation notes:
- Use ip target mode by default for minimal maintenance but allow instance mode for legacy customers.
- Prefer NLB TLS passthrough for high-throughput TCP workloads (KV cache replication) and ALB terminate+reencrypt for HTTP/HTTPS app routes requiring WAF and structured routing.
- Implement Terraform null_resource + local-exec hooks sparingly; prefer AWS provider resources and aws_alb_target_group_attachment to keep stateful attachments explicit.
- Add a terraform validate step that fails if estimated conntrack + ephemeral port usage (based on expected gRPC streams) exceeds node pool thresholds.

Success criteria:
- Module released in private-deployments repo and referenced by the private-install template.
- Automated canary deploys (50% -> 100%) complete without 5xx spike in 95th percentile latency in CI simulations.
- Runbook validated with on-call during staged rollout in a staging VPC.

acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes clear inputs for mode, scheme, tls_behavior, and az_balance and includes examples for both ip and instance target modes.
Blue/green upgrade runbook included and validated in staging with live traffic shift tooling (weights 0->50->100).
Automated terraform plan guard that aborts if conntrack estimate > available capacity unless 'force' flag set with explicit owner approval.
E2E test scenario simulating 1000 concurrent gRPC streams shows no more than 1% error-rate during a 5-minute rolling deploy in CI.
